shared_elements: monolithic stone pillar with broad flat carved face and projecting upper block (T-shaped head)
quadruped animal in profile with schematic bent legs
bare stone field surrounding the relief
excavation context with rubble/soil at base
justification: The most specific correspondence is that both are broad, flat-faced monolithic pillars with an overhanging upper block, carved in the same shallow, contour-outlined low relief, each including a profile quadruped with angular, schematic legs. The biggest difference is density and organisation: A is crowded with stacked registers of birds, snakes, figures and a banded zigzag frieze, whereas B carries a single isolated animal on an otherwise blank surface, so their compositional schemes hardly correspond.
